chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

One who recites Surah al-Ra'd frequently, Allah will never strike him with lightning, even if he is a Nāsibī ( enemy of the Ahl al-Bayt). And if he is a believer, he will be admitted to Paradise without reckoning, and intercession will be accepted for all those he knows from his family and his brothers.

key_terms.بِلَا حِسَابٍ: Without reckoning or counting of deeds
key_terms.سُورَةِ الرَّعْدِ: Surah al-Ra'd (The Thunder), the 13th chapter of the Quran
key_terms.نَاصِبِيًّا: Nāsibī, one who is hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues and rewards of reciting Surah al-Ra'd according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith emphasizes the protective power of Surah al-Ra'd, noting that its frequent recitation shields the reciter from lightning strikes even if they are a *Nasibi* (opponent of the Ahl al-Bayt). For the faithful, it guarantees entry into Paradise without reckoning (*bi-la hisab*) and grants intercession for their family and friends, highlighting the Surah's unique role in securing divine mercy and familial salvation.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from al-Hussain b. Abi al-’Ala from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) that he said: “

One who recites Surah Raad excessively, the Almighty Allah would never let him get struck by lightning even if that person is the enemy of Ahle Bayt (a.s.). If he is a believer He would make him enter Paradise and if he does intercession for his relatives and friends it would be accepted from him.”
